title: OS Grid Reference Distance Calculator
description: Measure projected-grid distance and bearing between the centres of two British grid reference squares.
summary_sentence: A grid-distance result is not a surveyed ground distance or walking route.
quick_answer: The tool converts two references to square centres and uses Pythagoras for projected-grid distance and grid bearing. Precision is limited by the referenced squares and projection; latitude/longitude output has no datum shift.

TQ 300 800 → easting 530,000, northing 180,000. TQ 330 840 → 533,000 and 184,000. Differences: 3,000 m east, 4,000 m north; distance = √(3,000² + 4,000²) = 5,000 m exactly.

Why not measure on the map with a ruler?
You can — the calculator is the same geometry without the ruler's parallax and the paper's stretch. Checking one against the other is good practice either way.

What datum sits under the grid?
OSGB36. GPS lat/lon (WGS84) for the same ground can sit up to roughly a hundred metres away from the grid's reading — the BNG helper explains the shift.
